title: 6 BORING Rental Businesses That Quietly Make Millionaires (Nobody Wants to Own One)

stated_problem.quote: Nobody buys a dumpster for 1 week of shingles.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Dumpster (skip) rental
idea.one_liner: Rent 20-yard roll-off dumpsters to roofers, remodelers and homeowners by the week, charging a weekly fee plus a charge for each ton over the limit
idea.customer: Roofers, remodelers, other contractors and homeowners doing cleanouts
idea.offer: Weekly roll-off dumpster dropped on site, then collected and the waste taken to landfill
idea.revenue_model: Weekly rental fee (~7 days included) plus a charge for each ton over the included weight

key_quotes.quote: Most operators get the first calls from contractors and a Google Business Profile with clear photos and a clear price.
a local roofer with a deadline wants someone who answers the phone on the first ring and drops the box before 7:00 in the morning.
A line in the contract with the included tonnage, usually about two tons, and a price for every ton over.
he called 10 roofers whose names were on his permit stack [music] and booked three drops for next month.

claims.quote: A 20-yd dumpster rents for roughly $275 to $700 a week.

acquisition_channels.details: Repeat business and referrals from contractors who are served reliably
Google Business Profile with clear photos and a clear price
Phoning roofers whose names appear on building permits

ideas.delivery: The owner-operator drops and collects dumpsters with a trailer pulled by a pickup (or a hook truck) and pays landfill fees; all physical work

uk_legal_risk.reason: Acquisition is contractor relationships, Google and phone calls. Cold-calling roofers (often sole traders) needs TPS/CTPS screening but is not banned. Do not switch to texting or DMing tradespeople.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK skip hire needs an Environment Agency waste carrier/broker registration and waste duty-of-care paperwork, plus council skip permits when skips go on the road; TPS/CTPS screening for cold calls

stated_problem.quote: A bride needs a clean restroom for one night.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Portable restroom and luxury restroom trailer rental
idea.one_liner: Rent standard portable toilets to job sites and luxury restroom trailers to weddings and events, charged per weekend or per event
idea.customer: Contractors and job sites; couples, wedding planners and venues without plumbing (barns, vineyards, backyards)
idea.offer: Standard portable units, or luxury restroom trailers delivered, serviced and collected
idea.revenue_model: Per-weekend or per-event rental, with a separate wedding rate card

key_quotes.quote: The venues that need these most are barns, vineyards, and backyards with no plumbing at all.
The trick that pays is a separate wedding rate card, so event weekends aren't priced like a job site.
Michael Vera Montes started The Lavatory in 2018 with two trailers.

claims.quote: Standard units rent for about $75 to $150 a weekend.

claims.claim: Luxury trailers rent for $500-$1,500 per event
claims.quote: Luxury trailers command about $500 to $1,500 per event.

claims.quote: a two-station trailer at about $769 per event, with about $619 kept after cleaning and supplies.

claims.quote: Four weddings a month is roughly $2,475 from one trailer.

claims.quote: By 2023, he had about 100, according to the trade magazine Pro Monthly.

claims.quote: Getting in usually means a new trailer at about $30,000 or $50,000 all in

claims.quote: One operator guide budgets about $800 a month in marketing to keep four wedding weekends booked.

claims.claim: Fleet owners keep about 20-25% of revenue
claims.quote: And fleet owners typically keep around 20 to 25% of revenue after everything.

About $800 a month marketing budget (channel not specified)

ideas.delivery: Owner tows trailers to sites, then services, pumps, refills water and cleans between events; all physical work
ideas.other_uk_rules: Disposing of the waste needs a waste carrier registration and licensed disposal; Consumer Rights Act 2015 for consumer bookings

stated_problem.quote: A family flies in for a week at the theme parks, and grandma can't walk 10 miles a day.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Mobility and medical equipment rental
idea.one_liner: Rent mobility scooters, wheelchairs and hospital beds to tourists and post-surgery families, delivered to hotels or homes, charged per day or week
idea.customer: Tourist families (theme parks, cruises) and families of patients discharged after surgery
idea.offer: Scooters, wheelchairs and hospital beds, delivered, collected and sanitised
idea.revenue_model: Per-rental-period fees (days for tourists, 3-6 weeks for medical)

key_quotes.quote: You need a handful of hotel concierges and one or two hospital discharge planners who know your number.
Most of the work is delivery, pickup, and cleaning between renters.
smart operators keep a card on file at pickup, so a scratched scooter never turns into an argument.

claims.claim: Walker Mobility charges $250-$335 for a 4-7 day scooter rental
claims.quote: Walker Mobility rents a mobility scooter for about 250 to 335 dollars for four to seven days, depending on the model.

claims.claim: 10 scooters rented 2 weeks a month at $250 a week is about $5,000 a month
claims.quote: 10 scooters, each rented two weeks a month at around 250 dollars a week is about 5,000 dollars a month.

claims.claim: A starter fleet costs from a few thousand dollars to about $10,000
claims.quote: A small starter fleet of scooters and wheelchairs usually runs from a few thousand to around $10,000, depending on new or used.

acquisition_channels.details: Relationships with hotel concierges and hospital discharge planners
Calling concierges and leaving cards with discharge planners

ideas.delivery: Owner stores the fleet in a garage or storage unit and delivers, collects and sanitises units by van
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR special-category data if health or discharge details are processed; Consumer Rights Act 2015; equipment safety and hygiene duties; hire contracts must be fair under consumer law

stated_problem.quote: They need the look for six hours.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Prop rental house
idea.one_liner: Rent furniture and props to film crews, photographers and event planners by the week, at 15-20% of each item's replacement value
idea.customer: Film and TV productions, photographers, event and wedding planners
idea.offer: A browsable catalogue of vintage furniture and props, rented weekly
idea.revenue_model: Weekly rent (15-20% of replacement value), long-rental discounts, deposits

key_quotes.quote: Film crews, photographers, and event planners rent furniture and props by the week.
Photograph and tag every piece the day you buy it, because a catalog nobody can browse doesn't get booked.

claims.claim: Weekly rent is 15-20% of replacement value
claims.quote: Weekly rent typically runs 15 to 20% of the item's replacement value.

claims.claim: A $500 sideboard could rent for $75-$100 a week
claims.quote: So, a vintage sideboard could rent for 75 to $100 a week if it's worth about 500.

claims.claim: An item pays for itself after 5-7 rented weeks
claims.quote: Five to seven rented weeks >> [music] >> and it has paid for itself.

claims.quote: Today, it calls itself the world's largest prop house with a 150,000 square-foot warehouse.

claims.claim: The start-up cost is a few thousand dollars of estate-sale finds
claims.quote: Most people start with a few thousand dollars of estate sale finds and a dry place to store them.

claims.claim: One prop house requires a $1,000 minimum deposit

claims.claim: Full price for week 1, half price for weeks 2-4

stated_problem.quote: Every traveler landing at your nearest airport, every couple who wants a convertible for an anniversary weekend, they need a car for 3 days.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Peer-to-peer car rental host (Turo)
idea.one_liner: List owned cars on Turo for travellers and special-occasion renters, keeping 70-90% of each trip
idea.offer: Cars rented by the day through Turo, priced under rental counters
idea.revenue_model: Daily rental fees minus a 10-30% platform cut, plus mileage overage fees

key_quotes.quote: List it, price it a little under the rental counters, and keep it spotless.
The smart move is a daily mileage limit with an overage rate in the listing.

claims.claim: The average Turo car earns about $906 a month
claims.quote: Turo says an average car [music] on its platform earns about $906 a month.

claims.claim: The host keeps 70/80/90% depending on the protection plan
claims.quote: The host keeps 70, 80, or 90% of each trip depending on the protection plan they pick.

claims.claim: About $634 a month at the lowest host share
claims.quote: That's about $634 a month at the lowest share from a car that would otherwise sit in a parking space.

claims.claim: Natalia Zarena had 69 cars by 2023
claims.quote: By 2023, she had 69 cars including a Ferrari and a Lamborghini.

claims.claim: Zarena earned $922,225 in one year (Business Insider)
claims.quote: Business Insider reported she earned $922,225 in 1 year verified with documents.

claims.claim: Her cheapest cars rent for $75 a day
claims.quote: Her cheapest cars rent for about $75 a day.

claims.quote: CNBC profiled Andre Echeverria who brings in up to $14,000 a month from six cars.

claims.claim: A used luxury car starts at about $30,000
claims.quote: A used luxury car usually starts somewhere around $30,000.

claims.claim: The platform keeps 10-30% of each trip
claims.quote: And the platform keeps 10 to 30% of every trip.

acquisition_channels.details: Listings on Turo priced below rental counters

ideas.delivery: Host hands over the cars (or uses remote handover), cleans, maintains and insures them; Turo handles booking and payment
ideas.other_uk_rules: Turo operates in the UK, but hosting needs suitable insurance and V5C/MOT compliance; a commercial fleet may need hire-and-reward insurance; UK GDPR for renter data

stated_problem.quote: They need the space for a few months and they absolutely don't want to buy a bigger house to hold it.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Self-storage facility
idea.one_liner: Own (usually by buying an existing) self-storage facility and rent units monthly to people who are moving or downsizing
idea.customer: Families moving, couples combining homes, people who have inherited belongings
idea.revenue_model: Monthly unit rent; quarterly rate increases; profit above about 80% occupancy

key_quotes.quote: That's why first-time owners often buy a small existing facility instead, usually with partners or a bank loan.
Smart operators review rates every quarter and raise them gently.

claims.claim: A 10x10 unit rents for $100-$200 a month (RecNation)
claims.quote: A 10 by 10 unit rents for about 100 to 200 dollars a month, according to the storage operator RecNation.

claims.claim: Facilities run 85-92% full in stable markets
claims.quote: In stable markets, facilities run about 85 to 92% full.

claims.claim: Break-even is around 80% occupancy
claims.quote: And the break-even point is around 80% occupancy.

claims.claim: 100 units at 90% full and $150 is about $13,500 a month
claims.quote: 100 units at 90% full at about $150 a month is around $13,500 a month in rent.

claims.claim: Operating costs are 35-50% of revenue
claims.quote: Operating costs typically run 35 to 50% of revenue, so roughly half could be left before any loan payments.

claims.claim: Public Storage founders each put in $25,000 in 1972
claims.quote: In 1972, Wayne Hughes and Ken Volk each put in $25,000 and opened one storage facility in El Cajon, California.

claims.claim: Hughes was worth about $3.3B in 2021 (Forbes)
claims.quote: Forbes put Hughes at about $3.3 billion in 2021.

claims.claim: A new 200-400 unit build costs $2-5M
claims.quote: Building a 200 to 400 unit facility from the ground up runs about two to five million dollars according to Raconteur.

acquisition_channels.details: Visible signage near highways (orange doors); local demand from people moving nearby
Implied local search ('search' named as a renter-reach channel)

ideas.delivery: Facility with on-site or remote management; tenants access their own units; the owner handles maintenance, pricing and collections
ideas.other_uk_rules: Planning permission/zoning, business rates, Consumer Rights Act and unfair-terms rules on rent increases and lien clauses; UK GDPR for tenant data and CCTV
